name_ru: Пожар на заводе Philips в Альбукерке (2000)
name_en: Philips Albuquerque RF chip plant fire (2000)
shock_mechanism: Fire at Philips Albuquerque RF-chip fab forced ~3-week total shutdown; line still at only ~50% of pre-fire capacity 6 months later
channels: Single-source RF chip dependency for mobile-handset makers (Ericsson, Nokia)

notes: NOT WIRED - data-quality gap, not a graph-coverage gap (NLD:semiconductors, DEU:electronics, USA:electronics are all valid GEDS nodes). (1) The only sourced magnitude (50% of pre-fire capacity) is measured at the 6-month/26-week mark - a residual still-impaired level, not the peak; the actual peak (full closure) lasted the first ~3 weeks and implies a much larger trough that the research did not separately quantify. (2) No global/industry-wide pct figure exists (contrast renesas-naka-fire-2021's IHS-sourced 1.6% of global auto production) - only company-specific absolutes ($400M Ericsson sales loss, 7M handsets) - so HISTORICAL_EVENTS' required observed.auto_production_loss_pct cannot be populated without fabricating a global ratio. (3) Ericsson is Swedish; Sweden has no GEDS node, so DEU:electronics was floated as an 'approximate' downstream proxy - this is a country misattribution, not an approximation, and must not be written into cascade_spatial.csv as a DEU event. (4) The proposed USA:electronics downstream effect actually describes Nokia avoiding loss via resupply (a non-cascade resilience result), not an output_loss - labeling it as such would invert the finding. Park pending either a sourced global handset/electronics industry-wide loss pct, or an explicit decision to calibrate only the node-level NLD:semiconductors magnitude from the two-point (peak~1.0 at week 0-3, ~0.50 at week 26) shape.

shock_mechanism: FAA emergency airworthiness directive (Mar 13 2019) grounded the 737 MAX worldwide; Boeing cut output 52->42/month, then fully suspended MAX production Jan-May 2020; deliveries resumed after FAA rescission Nov 18 2020
channels: Single-program delivery halt cascading to Boeing's airframe supply base (Spirit AeroSystems)
sources: Boeing official delivery data via Argus Media 2020-01-13 (806 in 2018 -> 380 in 2019); Boeing Investor Relations production-suspension press release 2019-12-16; Boeing Q2 2019 earnings (Reuters/NPR 2019-07-24); Supply Chain Dive 2020-06-24 citing Spirit AeroSystems SEC filing; Aviation Week 2020-11-29 (Airbus+Boeing deliveries 1,583->1,150)
notes: NOT WIRED - graph-structure + Track-A gap. Unlike Philips, the PRIMARY node mapping is correct (USA:aerospace; Boeing is American) and the downstream cascade is correctly directional (Spirit AeroSystems output loss, not inverted). Blocked by a more fundamental limit: (1) GRAPH CANNOT REPRESENT THE OFFSET - the 737 MAX grounding's GLOBAL aerospace impact stayed small precisely because Airbus (FRA, no graph node) ramped A320neo to absorb the demand. The graph holds only USA:aerospace (89.0% of in-graph aerospace GDP) and DEU:aerospace (11.0%); with no France/Airbus node it structurally overstates global aerospace loss and has no sourced figure to validate against. (2) NO TRACK A - no tier-1 body (FAA/IATA/ICAO/AIA) published a global aerospace output-loss %; the best available (Aviation Week Airbus+Boeing deliveries -27%) is a two-firm duopoly number, not industry-body-sourced, and overstates the broad aerospace industry (defense/space/engines/MRO unaffected). (3) MAGNITUDE CONFLATION - proposed peak_magnitude 1.0 on USA:aerospace describes the 737 MAX PROGRAM (100% delivery halt), not the node: Boeing kept building 787/777/defense and other US primes (Lockheed, Northrop, GE Aviation) were largely untouched. Even the research's own Track B 0.53 is Boeing-commercial-deliveries YoY, a sub-component of the node. (4) DEU:aerospace downstream is a flagged proxy standing in for French Safran (no France node). POSITIVES recorded for future use: first regulatory-cliff (step, weeks_to_peak=0) event; CALIBRATION_GRADE node sourcing (Boeing official deliveries 806->380 = -52.9% [DERIVED]); would be the first aerospace calibration anchor (aerospace is currently uncalibrated). Unblock path: a tier-1 global aerospace output figure AND a France/Airbus node to model the duopoly offset, OR an explicit decision to calibrate node-level-only with a corrected (sub-1.0) USA:aerospace magnitude reflecting Boeing-commercial's share of the node.

A measured source-side output decline DOES exist (China NBS -11.6% YoY, rare for a semiconductor node, unlike TWN where output grew) at the untapped GOOD-tier node CHN:semiconductors. BUT it is a DEMAND-driven contraction (chip glut, not shortage) — the OPPOSITE causal direction to the engine's supply-cascade model (same structural class as the GFC demand collapse), so wiring it as a supply shock would misrepresent the physics. Attribution is also mixed (export controls + zero-COVID + demand + Ukraine). Needs a demand-side mechanism (future work) before it can be added to the calibration set.
